summary: This example validates the reusable report template, hierarchy, tables, callouts, pagination and the current public-reference EUROIMMUN header. It contains no project-confidential facts.

blocks.text: The document renderer keeps substantive content separate from layout. A report specification can therefore be reused for DOCX and PDF output without maintaining two independent visual systems.

blocks.title: Decision posture
blocks.text: Template architecture is suitable for controlled internal working reports. For formal external documents, an approved current corporate template should be supplied through the template override.

rows: Structured source package and performance data

blocks.title: Open item
blocks.text: The public-reference header is not a substitute for an internally controlled corporate letterhead where document control requires one.

This paragraph intentionally contains enough text to exercise line wrapping and spacing. The renderer should preserve a restrained corporate appearance with generous white space, a clear green accent, black body text and a stable header and footer on every page. Long reports should remain readable without manual spacing hacks or hard-coded page coordinates.

blocks.text: When an approved internal EUROIMMUN template is available, it should replace the bundled public-reference template via --template. The renderer validates required placeholders and fails clearly if the supplied template is incompatible instead of silently reverting to another letterhead.
